description: OKLab and OKLCh. The transform is Ottosson (2020); the CONSTANTS are CSS Color 4's recalculation of it for a consistent reference white (csswg-drafts issue 6642), which is what makes D65 white land on (1, 0, 0) instead of at chroma 1.25e-4. See ADR-0040. The first entries are the matrix elements themselves, at tolerance 0. That is where the real discrimination lives, and it is worth being precise about why: Ottosson's published test table passes with BOTH candidate constant sets — his original ten-decimal matrices AND CSS Color 4's recalculation — and on two of its four rows ours is the further away of the two. Those entries verify that the transform is the right transform; they cannot choose between the constant sets, and they already sit at 40% of their tolerance. What discriminates is the digit-for-digit matrix entries, the d65-white-is-exactly-neutral entry at 1e-15 (which Ottosson's originals fail by 1.25e-4), and bitwise agreement with colorjs.io.

entries.derivationNote: XYZ = [0.20343667060423742, 0.21404114048223255, 0.23310316302365935]. L = 0.598 against CIELAB's L* = 53.4 for the same colour: OKLab lightness is on [0,1] and is NOT CIELAB lightness divided by 100. a and b are at the float64 floor rather than exactly zero, because the XYZ input is a scaled white whose ratios are not bit-identical.

entries.source: Ottosson (2020) — OKLCh is OKLab in polar form; C = hypot(a, b), h = atan2(b, a)
Ottosson (2020) — OKLab in polar form; b is negative so the raw angle folds
Ottosson (2020) — OKLCh is OKLab in polar form, and hue is undefined at zero chroma
entries.derivationNote: D65 white gives OKLab a = -4.996e-16, b = +0, so atan2(+0, -4.996e-16) is pi and the hue reads 180 degrees. Mid grey reads 189.46. Both are arbitrary and both are HARMLESS at C = 5e-16 — but F-014 rotates hue in OKLCh, and a caller that reads h from a near-neutral and re-applies it at C = 0.1 gets cyan out of white. Pinned so the behaviour is a recorded fact rather than a surprise, and so a future change to it is visible. CHECK CHROMA BEFORE HUE.
